title: Exact Recovery for Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Sakura Schafer-Nameki
abstract: We study exact recovery for non-Abelian topological surface codes based on the quantum double $D(G)$ of any finite group $G$. We determine an orthogonal error basis, that is comprised of group multiplication and irreducible representation operators. Whenever the errors are supported on closed loops on the lattice or dual lattice, there is a redundancy in the basis, due to stabilizers. To remedy this, we introduce a gauge-fixing that results in a complete and orthogonal error basis on the code space. Assuming as input predetermined, neutral correctable error clusters, we construct charge and flux transfer circuits that move the errors onto ancillas that then get projected out. This is an exact and deterministic recovery protocol, applicable to surface codes for any finite, in particular non-Abelian, group $G$.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive, deterministic quantum error correction protocol for non-Abelian topological surface codes defined by the quantum double D(G). It constructs a complete error basis and details a systematic recovery mechanism using charge and flux transfer circuits. This work is significant because it moves beyond merely proving the existence of such a code to providing the explicit, implementable circuit for fault tolerance in complex quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing an exact and deterministic quantum error correction (QEC) protocol for non-Abelian topological surface codes.
main_result: They construct a complete and orthogonal error basis and detail a deterministic recovery protocol involving charge and flux transfer circuits applicable to any finite group G.
method: The methodology involves generalizing the Pauli error basis using group multiplication and irreducible representation operators, followed by introducing a gauge-fixing procedure to ensure orthogonality and completeness.
model_or_system: The system is a non-Abelian topological surface code based on the quantum double D(G) of a finite group G. The Hamiltonian is defined by vertex and plaquette operators, and the code space is the $+1$ eigenspace of this Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Error detection is diagnosed via plaquette violations (flux) and vertex violations (charge), which are measured using generalized operators.
important_parameters: The protocol is applicable for any finite group G, including non-Abelian groups.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the input errors are predetermined, neutral, and correctable clusters, leaving the optimal syndrome extraction/decoder construction for future work.
figures_summary: Figure 5 illustrates the structure of a ribbon ($\xi$) with $n=3$, detailing its support edges and end vertices, which is central to the error analysis.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the error basis for D(G) (including irrep operators) to analyzing local error detection (flux/charge checks) and culminates in a detailed, systematic protocol for recovering errors supported on extended structures called 'ribbons.'
why_interesting: The explicit construction of a deterministic recovery circuit for non-Abelian codes is a major theoretical advance, providing concrete tools for fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond simple Pauli noise models.
